official_measurement_examples.name: Act commencement and geography
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Party Wall etc. Act 1996 came into force on 1 July 1997 and applies in England and Wales.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 2 notice period
official_measurement_examples.fact: The official booklet states notice for work to an existing party wall or structure is generally served at least 2 months before work starts.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 1 and 6 notice period
official_measurement_examples.fact: The official flowchart gives one month for new party walls or structures at boundaries and for excavation notices.

official_measurement_examples.name: Fourteen-day response window
official_measurement_examples.fact: The booklet explains that where written consent is not received within 14 days in specified cases, a dispute is treated as having arisen for the Act's surveyor procedure.

official_measurement_examples.name: Three-metre excavation test
official_measurement_examples.fact: The booklet identifies excavation within 3 metres where work goes deeper than the neighbour's foundations as a section 6 scenario.

official_measurement_examples.name: Six-metre excavation test
official_measurement_examples.fact: The booklet also identifies a 6 metre test using a 45-degree line from the bottom of neighbouring foundations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Award boundary limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The official booklet states Party Wall surveyors cannot determine a dispute about the location of the boundary.

official_measurement_examples.name: Court remedy caveat
official_measurement_examples.fact: The booklet notes that starting covered work without notice can expose a building owner to an injunction or other legal redress.
